```{r setup, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>", fig.width = 7, fig.height = 4.5)
library(nlmixr2lib)
library(PKNCA)
library(rxode2)
library(dplyr)
library(ggplot2)
```

# Model and source

Weiss 2023 studied nebulized niclosamide ethanolamine (NEN), an inhaled
formulation of the oral anthelminthic niclosamide, in healthy ewes. Plasma
concentrations after three nebulized doses and one intravenous infusion were
fitted simultaneously with a three-compartment population PK model in NONMEM
(FOCE+I), which estimates the absolute bioavailability of the nebulized dose.
Epithelial lining fluid (ELF) concentrations and the oral arm were analysed by
non-compartmental methods only (the paper reports that no ELF model could be
established), so they are not part of the model.

* Article: <https://doi.org/10.1007/s11095-023-03559-0>
* Open access: <https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/pmc/articles/PMC10447587/>

```{r model}
mod <- readModelDb("Weiss_2023_niclosamide_sheep")
mod_ui <- rxode2::rxode2(mod)
mod_ui
```

# Population

Ten 12-month-old Merino cross-bred ewes in two cohorts of five (Table I). The
nebulized cohort (sheep 1-5, 25-35 kg) received a placebo and then 10, 30 and
60 mg NEN by an in-line eFlow nebulizer through an endotracheal tube, over
24-27 min, with 7-day washouts. The second cohort (sheep 11-14 and 18,
40.6 +/- 2.1 kg) received 1132 mg oral niclosamide and a 3 mg intravenous NEN
infusion over 30 min. Plasma was sampled at 14 time points over 12 h (Table I).
Only the nebulized and intravenous plasma data enter the population PK model.

# Source trace

| Model element | Value | Source |
|---|---|---|
| Structure: absorption compartment, central, shallow and deep peripheral | -- | Methods, "Non-compartmental and compartmental Pharmacokinetic analysis", equations for dAabs/dt, dA1/dt, dA2/dt, dA3/dt |
| Nebulized input: zero-order into the absorption compartment | over the nebulization time | Methods, same section ("time-delimited zero-order ... input") |
| IV input: zero-order into central | 3 mL at 0.1 mL/min (30 min) | Methods, "Niclosamide administration procedures"; Table S1 |
| `lka` | 20.9 1/h | Table S2; Table II |
| `lfdepot` (Fneb) | 85.8% | Table S2 (Table II rounds to 86%) |
| `lcl` | 170 L/h | Table S2 |
| `lvc` (V1) | 15.7 L | Table S2 |
| `lvp` (V2, shallow) | 10.1 L | Table S2 |
| `lq` (CLd1) | 57.4 L/h | Table S2 |
| `lvp2` (V3, deep) | 148 L | Table S2 |
| `lq2` (CLd2) | 7.47 L/h | Table S2 |
| `etalka` | 76% CV | Table S2 |
| `etalcl` | 34% CV | Table S2 |
| `etalvc` | 71% CV | Table S2 |
| `etalvp` | 28% CV | Table S2 |
| `propSd` | 25.2% | Table S2 |
| `addSd` | 0.26 ng/mL | Table S2 |
| Half-lives (validation target) | 0.041, 0.2, 14 h | Table II; Results text |
| Plasma NCA (validation target) | Cmax, Tmax, AUC0-t | Table II |

# Typical-value checks

## Disposition half-lives

Table II reports half-lives of 0.041 h (alpha), 0.2 h (beta) and 14 h
(terminal). These are the eigenvalues of the typical-value disposition
matrix, so they follow from CL, V1, V2, V3, CLd1 and CLd2 alone.

```{r half-lives}
th <- exp(mod_ui$theta)
kel <- th[["lcl"]] / th[["lvc"]]
k12 <- th[["lq"]] / th[["lvc"]]
k21 <- th[["lq"]] / th[["lvp"]]
k13 <- th[["lq2"]] / th[["lvc"]]
k31 <- th[["lq2"]] / th[["lvp2"]]
disp <- matrix(
  c(-(kel + k12 + k13), k21, k31,
    k12, -k21, 0,
    k13, 0, -k31),
  nrow = 3, byrow = TRUE
)
thalf <- sort(log(2) / -eigen(disp)$values)
data.frame(
  phase = c("alpha", "beta", "terminal"),
  model_h = signif(thalf, 3),
  published_h = c(0.041, 0.2, 14)
) |>
  knitr::kable(caption = "Typical-value half-lives versus Table II.")

# The parameters are deterministic here, so the comparison is a rounding check.
stopifnot(
  abs(thalf[1] - 0.041) < 0.0005,
  abs(thalf[2] - 0.2) < 0.025,
  abs(thalf[3] - 14) < 0.5
)
```

## Nebulized bioavailability and dose linearity

The dose-normalised typical-value AUC0-inf of a nebulized dose relative to the
intravenous dose recovers Fneb, and the model is linear in dose (the paper
reports dose-linear plasma PK across 10-60 mg NEN, Fig. S3).

```{r bioavailability}
mod_typ <- rxode2::zeroRe(mod_ui)
ev_typ <- rbind(
  data.frame(id = 1L, time = 0, amt = 10, dur = 27 / 60, evid = 1L, cmt = "depot"),
  data.frame(id = 2L, time = 0, amt = 60, dur = 25 / 60, evid = 1L, cmt = "depot"),
  data.frame(id = 3L, time = 0, amt = 3, dur = 0.5, evid = 1L, cmt = "central")
)
obs_typ <- expand.grid(id = 1:3, time = c(seq(0, 2, by = 0.005), seq(2.05, 400, by = 0.05)))
obs_typ <- transform(obs_typ, amt = 0, dur = 0, evid = 0L, cmt = "central")
sim_typ <- rxode2::rxSolve(mod_typ, rbind(ev_typ, obs_typ), returnType = "data.frame")

auc_typ <- sim_typ |>
  dplyr::group_by(id) |>
  dplyr::summarise(
    cmax = max(Cc),
    auc = sum(diff(time) * (head(Cc, -1) + tail(Cc, -1)) / 2)
  ) |>
  dplyr::mutate(dose = c(10, 60, 3), auc_per_mg = auc / dose)
f_neb <- auc_typ$auc_per_mg[1] / auc_typ$auc_per_mg[3]
knitr::kable(auc_typ, digits = 3, caption = "Typical-value exposure (AUC to 400 h).")
f_neb

stopifnot(
  # AUC(nebulized)/AUC(IV), dose-normalised, equals Fneb = 0.858.
  abs(f_neb - 0.858) < 0.01,
  # Linear model: 60 mg and 10 mg give the same dose-normalised AUC.
  abs(auc_typ$auc_per_mg[2] / auc_typ$auc_per_mg[1] - 1) < 0.01
)
```

# Which dose to enter: nominal or delivered

The nebulizer was charged with 10, 30 or 60 mg NEN, but drug left in the
nebulizer, lines and expiratory filters was rinsed out and assayed so that the
actual delivered dose could be calculated (Methods). Table S1 reports the
delivered doses as 0.271, 0.762 and 1.401 mg/kg; for ewes of 25-35 kg that is
roughly 70-80% of the nominal charge. The intravenous dose (0.073 mg/kg in
40.6 kg ewes, 2.96 mg) has no such loss.

The paper does not say which of the two entered the modelling data set, but
its own model simulations settle it. The median (P50) curves of Figure S3 were
digitised by the maintainers at 2-5 h, where they are clear of the observed
points, and compared with the typical-value prediction for the nominal doses:

```{r dose-basis}
# Figure S3 P50, digitised by the maintainers against the 0.5 ng/mL LLOQ line
# (which reads back as 0.495 ng/mL). Time is from the start of nebulization.
fig_s3 <- data.frame(
  nominal_mg = c(10, 10, 10, 10, 30, 30, 30, 60, 60, 60, 60),
  time = c(2, 3, 4, 4.9, 3, 4, 4.9, 2, 3, 4, 4.9),
  p50_fig = c(0.18, 0.075, 0.062, 0.062, 0.20, 0.16, 0.16, 0.95, 0.41, 0.35, 0.33)
)
neb_dur <- c(`10` = 27, `30` = 24, `60` = 25) / 60
ev_nom <- do.call(rbind, lapply(seq_along(neb_dur), function(i) {
  rbind(
    data.frame(id = i, time = 0, amt = as.numeric(names(neb_dur)[i]),
               dur = neb_dur[[i]], evid = 1L, cmt = "depot"),
    data.frame(id = i, time = c(2, 3, 4, 4.9), amt = 0, dur = 0, evid = 0L,
               cmt = "central")
  )
}))
typ_nom <- rxode2::rxSolve(mod_typ, ev_nom, returnType = "data.frame") |>
  dplyr::mutate(nominal_mg = as.numeric(names(neb_dur))[id]) |>
  dplyr::select(nominal_mg, time, Cc_nominal = Cc)
dose_basis <- dplyr::inner_join(fig_s3, typ_nom, by = c("nominal_mg", "time")) |>
  dplyr::mutate(ratio = p50_fig / Cc_nominal)
knitr::kable(dose_basis, digits = 3,
             caption = "Figure S3 P50 versus the typical-value prediction for the nominal nebulizer charge.")
summary(dose_basis$ratio)

# The paper's simulations sit well below a nominal-dose simulation in every
# dose group, so the data set did not carry the nominal charge.
stopifnot(median(dose_basis$ratio) < 0.85)
```

Figure S3 lies 0.6-0.75 times below the nominal-dose prediction in all three
groups and at every time, which is the size of the delivery loss. The model
should therefore be dosed with the **delivered** nebulized dose. The
simulations below use the Table S1 mean delivered dose in mg/kg multiplied by
30 kg, the middle of the 25-35 kg weight range of the nebulized cohort.

# Virtual cohort and simulation

One hundred virtual ewes per arm receive each of the four modelled regimens.
Nebulization times are the Table S1 means (27, 24 and 25 min for the 10, 30
and 60 mg doses); the IV dose is a 30 min infusion. Plasma is sampled on the
Table I schedule: before dosing, at 7.5 and 15 min during dosing, and at 0, 5,
15 and 30 min and 1, 2, 3, 4, 6, 8 and 12 h after the end of dosing. A dense
grid is added for the figure.

```{r cohort}
arms <- data.frame(
  treatment = c("0.167% NEN nebulized", "0.5% NEN nebulized",
                "1% NEN nebulized", "0.1% NEN intravenous"),
  nominal_mg = c(10, 30, 60, 3),
  # Table S1 delivered dose (mg/kg) x 30 kg for the nebulized cohort and
  # x 40.6 kg (Table I footnote) for the intravenous cohort.
  amt = c(0.271 * 30, 0.762 * 30, 1.401 * 30, 0.073 * 40.6),
  dur_min = c(27, 24, 25, 30),
  cmt = c("depot", "depot", "depot", "central")
)
knitr::kable(arms, digits = 2, caption = "Simulated regimens (amt = delivered dose, mg NEN).")
arms$treatment <- factor(arms$treatment, levels = arms$treatment)
n_per_arm <- 100L
post_end_h <- c(0, 5, 15, 30, 60, 120, 180, 240, 360, 480, 720) / 60

make_arm <- function(i, n, id_offset) {
  a <- arms[i, ]
  ids <- id_offset + seq_len(n)
  dur <- a$dur_min / 60
  sched <- sort(unique(c(0, 7.5 / 60, 15 / 60, dur + post_end_h)))
  grid <- seq(0, dur + 12, by = 1 / 60)
  sched <- round(sched, 6)
  obs_times <- sort(unique(round(c(sched, grid), 6)))
  dose <- data.frame(id = ids, time = 0, amt = a$amt, dur = dur, evid = 1L,
                     cmt = a$cmt, treatment = a$treatment, scheduled = FALSE)
  obs <- expand.grid(id = ids, time = obs_times)
  obs$amt <- 0
  obs$dur <- 0
  obs$evid <- 0L
  obs$cmt <- "central"
  obs$treatment <- a$treatment
  obs$scheduled <- obs$time %in% sched
  rbind(dose, obs)
}
events <- do.call(rbind, lapply(seq_len(nrow(arms)), function(i) {
  make_arm(i, n_per_arm, (i - 1L) * n_per_arm)
}))
events <- events[order(events$id, events$time, -events$evid), ]
stopifnot(!anyDuplicated(events[events$evid == 1, "id"]))

rxode2::rxSetSeed(20230727)
sim <- rxode2::rxSolve(mod_ui, events, keep = c("treatment", "scheduled"),
                       returnType = "data.frame")
```

# Replicate Figure 2A

```{r fig2a, fig.height = 5}
llq <- 0.5
sim |>
  dplyr::group_by(treatment, time) |>
  dplyr::summarise(
    p05 = quantile(Cc, 0.05), p50 = median(Cc), p95 = quantile(Cc, 0.95),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) |>
  dplyr::filter(time > 0, time <= 3) |>
  ggplot(aes(time, p50, colour = treatment, fill = treatment)) +
  geom_ribbon(aes(ymin = p05, ymax = p95), alpha = 0.15, colour = NA) +
  geom_line() +
  geom_hline(yintercept = llq, linetype = "dashed") +
  scale_y_log10() +
  labs(x = "Time after start of dosing (h)", y = "Plasma niclosamide (ng/mL)",
       colour = NULL, fill = NULL) +
  theme_bw() +
  theme(legend.position = "bottom")
```

Replicates Figure 2A (semilog panel) of Weiss 2023: median and 90% prediction
interval of plasma niclosamide by dose group; dashed line is the 0.5 ng/mL
LLOQ. As in the paper, concentrations peak at the end of nebulization, fall
steeply over the first 1-2 h and approach the LLOQ by 1-2 h for the 10 mg dose,
with the IV profile tracking the 10 mg nebulized profile.

# Replicate Figure S3

```{r fig-s3, fig.height = 4}
sim_p50 <- sim |>
  dplyr::filter(treatment != "0.1% NEN intravenous") |>
  dplyr::mutate(nominal_mg = arms$nominal_mg[match(treatment, arms$treatment)]) |>
  dplyr::group_by(nominal_mg, treatment, time) |>
  dplyr::summarise(
    P10 = quantile(Cc, 0.1), P50 = median(Cc), P90 = quantile(Cc, 0.9),
    .groups = "drop"
  )
fig_s3_lab <- fig_s3 |>
  dplyr::mutate(treatment = arms$treatment[match(nominal_mg, arms$nominal_mg)])
sim_p50 |>
  dplyr::filter(time > 0, time <= 5) |>
  tidyr::pivot_longer(c(P10, P50, P90), names_to = "percentile", values_to = "Cc") |>
  ggplot(aes(time, Cc)) +
  geom_line(aes(linetype = percentile)) +
  geom_point(data = fig_s3_lab, aes(time, p50_fig), colour = "red") +
  geom_hline(yintercept = llq, linetype = "dotted") +
  facet_wrap(~treatment) +
  scale_y_log10() +
  labs(x = "Time (h)", y = "Plasma niclosamide (ng/mL)", linetype = NULL) +
  theme_bw() +
  theme(legend.position = "bottom")

s3_check <- dplyr::inner_join(
  fig_s3,
  sim_p50 |> dplyr::mutate(time = round(time, 4)),
  by = c("nominal_mg", "time")
) |>
  dplyr::mutate(ratio = P50 / p50_fig)
knitr::kable(dplyr::select(s3_check, nominal_mg, time, p50_fig, P50, ratio), digits = 3,
             caption = "Simulated P50 (delivered doses) versus the digitised Figure S3 P50.")

stopifnot(
  nrow(s3_check) == nrow(fig_s3),
  abs(log(median(s3_check$ratio))) < log(1.3)
)
```

Replicates Figure S3 of Weiss 2023 (P10, P50 and P90 of the model simulations
by dose group); red points are the digitised published P50. With the delivered
doses the simulated median comes within about 20% of the published one (median
ratio near 1.2). The remaining gap is the size of either a lighter cohort
(about 25 kg rather than 30 kg) or a salt-to-base correction of the doses
(factor 0.84), which this comparison cannot separate.

# PKNCA validation

The paper's NCA (PKSolver) used the scheduled samples above the LLOQ, so the
simulated individual predictions are taken on the Table I schedule and samples
below 0.5 ng/mL are dropped before the NCA. The pre-dose sample is kept as
zero.

```{r pknca}
sim_nca <- sim |>
  dplyr::filter(scheduled) |>
  dplyr::mutate(Cc = ifelse(time > 0 & Cc < llq, NA_real_, Cc)) |>
  dplyr::filter(!is.na(Cc)) |>
  dplyr::select(id, time, Cc, treatment)
stopifnot(all(sim_nca$Cc[sim_nca$time == 0] == 0))
stopifnot(length(unique(sim_nca$id[sim_nca$time == 0])) == nrow(arms) * n_per_arm)

conc_obj <- PKNCA::PKNCAconc(sim_nca, Cc ~ time | treatment + id)
dose_df <- events |>
  dplyr::filter(evid == 1) |>
  dplyr::select(id, time, amt, dur, treatment)
dose_obj <- PKNCA::PKNCAdose(dose_df, amt ~ time | treatment + id, duration = "dur")

intervals <- data.frame(start = 0, end = Inf, cmax = TRUE, tmax = TRUE, auclast = TRUE)
nca_res <- PKNCA::pk.nca(PKNCA::PKNCAdata(conc_obj, dose_obj, intervals = intervals))
```

## Comparison against published NCA

Table II reports the mean of the observed NCA parameters for the nebulized
groups (Tmax converted from min to h below); no plasma NCA is tabulated for the
intravenous arm. `ncaComparisonTable()` summarises the simulated cohort by its
median.

```{r nca-compare}
published <- data.frame(
  treatment = c("0.167% NEN nebulized", "0.5% NEN nebulized", "1% NEN nebulized"),
  cmax = c(76.6, 239.8, 577.1),
  tmax = c(27.1, 24.3, 22.2) / 60,
  auclast = c(35.9, 96.1, 261.4)
)

cmp <- nlmixr2lib::ncaComparisonTable(
  simulated = nca_res,
  reference = published,
  by = "treatment",
  units = c(cmax = "ng/mL", tmax = "h", auclast = "ng*h/mL"),
  tolerance_pct = 20
)
knitr::kable(cmp, caption = "Simulated (median) vs. published (mean, Table II) plasma NCA. * differs from reference by >20%.")
```

```{r nca-assert}
sim_med <- as.data.frame(nca_res$result) |>
  dplyr::filter(PPTESTCD %in% c("cmax", "auclast"),
                treatment %in% published$treatment) |>
  dplyr::group_by(treatment, PPTESTCD) |>
  dplyr::summarise(med = median(PPORRES), .groups = "drop") |>
  tidyr::pivot_wider(names_from = PPTESTCD, values_from = med) |>
  dplyr::left_join(published, by = "treatment", suffix = c("_sim", "_pub"))
sim_med

# Structural check on the centre of the distribution: a mis-transcribed CL,
# volume, Fneb or dose unit moves these ratios by far more than the band.
stopifnot(
  all(sim_med$cmax_sim / sim_med$cmax_pub > 0.67 & sim_med$cmax_sim / sim_med$cmax_pub < 1.5),
  all(sim_med$auclast_sim / sim_med$auclast_pub > 0.67 & sim_med$auclast_sim / sim_med$auclast_pub < 1.5)
)
```

Rows starred in the table (typically the 1% Cmax, about 25% low, and the 0.5%
AUC0-t, about 20% high) go in opposite directions across groups: the
observed means are not dose-proportional (Cmax per mg NEN 7.7, 8.0 and 9.6;
AUC0-t per mg 3.6, 3.2 and 4.4), whereas the model is linear, as the paper
concluded from its population analysis. The simulated medians are compared with observed arithmetic means of five
sheep per group, whose standard deviations in Table II are 20-38% of the mean
for Cmax and 29-32% for AUC0-t, and from which eight implausible data points
were excluded before the NCA (Fig. 2 legend). The simulated doses also rest on
an assumed 30 kg body weight. Differences of the order of 20-30% are therefore
within the precision of the published values.

# Assumptions and deviations

- **Delivered, not nominal, nebulized dose.** The paper does not state which
  dose entered the modelling data set. Its own Figure S3 simulations sit
  0.6-0.75 times below a nominal-dose simulation in every group, matching the
  delivery loss implied by Table S1, so the model is dosed with the delivered
  dose. The individual body weights of the nebulized cohort are not reported;
  the vignette uses 30 kg, the middle of the stated 25-35 kg range.
- **Salt basis.** Doses are entered in mg of niclosamide ethanolamine (NEN),
  the unit the paper reports for every dose (Table I, Table S1). The paper
  does not state a salt correction before modelling. If the data set used
  niclosamide-equivalent doses instead (NEN is about 84% niclosamide by mass),
  CL and the volumes would be about 16% lower on a NEN-dose basis; Fneb is
  unaffected because both routes share the same basis. The Figure S3
  comparison cannot separate the two, because the unknown body weights
  (25-35 kg) move the delivered dose by more than 16%.
- **IIV scale.** Table S2 reports IIV as %CV for a log-normal model; the
  variances are omega^2 = log(CV^2 + 1). Table S2 lists no covariance, so the
  etas are independent (the paper tested a CL-V covariance during model
  building).
- **Bioavailability placement.** The paper writes Fneb on the
  absorption-to-central flux (ka * Fneb * Aabs). The model applies it to the
  nebulized dose (`f(depot)`), which gives identical central, peripheral and
  plasma amounts.
- **Nebulization time.** The zero-order nebulized input uses the Table S1 mean
  delivery time per dose group in this vignette; the paper used the individual
  recorded delivery times.
- **Out of scope.** No ELF model was established and the oral arm was not
  modelled (Results; Discussion), so neither appears here. The deep peripheral
  parameters had RSE above 100% (Table S2 footnote); the paper cautions against
  extrapolating beyond 3 h for regimens outside those studied.
- **Errata.** No correction notice was found for this article (Europe PMC,
  checked 2026-10-27).
